comparator.route: Ordinary three-year Chemistry bachelor with minimum 12-EC chemistry electives and 27-EC open electives in year three
comparator.sourceNotes: Official prospective pages total 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one has 60 EC required molecular chemistry, analysis and synthesis labs, mathematics and supporting physics; the 0-EC Academic Skills listing is excluded. Year two has 60 EC required organic/inorganic and physical chemistry, quantum mechanics, mathematics/data, microscopy and synthesis lab. Year three comprises 6 EC required writing and academic skills, 3 EC from one of two philosophy/ethics options, 12 EC required independent research internship/report, and 39 EC elective space of which at least 12 EC must come from published Chemistry electives. For a neutral concrete route, select the first two 6-EC chemistry electives listed (RNA Structure and Function and Magnetic Resonance I), leaving the other 27 EC genuinely open. The chemistry elective list cautions that offerings vary by year; the prospective route is indicative and course enrolment needs checking. The optional education minor and other 15–30 EC minors are not compulsory and are not counted in addition to the 39 EC choice space.

routeSelection.basis: The generic programme has no formal named specialization. Two first feasible 6-EC Chemistry electives on the official list supply the minimum 12 EC without optimizing against UCR. One first listed philosophy/ethics option supplies the required 3 EC. The remaining 27 EC remain genuinely free.

exception.reason: The defining 120 EC in years one and two is chemistry and laboratory centred: analytical, organic and inorganic chemistry; molecular structure and bonding; thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and physics; successive chemical synthesis and analysis laboratories. In year three, at least 12 EC of chemistry electives and a 12-EC independent chemistry research internship/report remain required. Although 27 EC can be freely chosen, UCR lacks a chemistry gateway and any stand-alone introductory or advanced organic, inorganic, analytical, physical or synthetic chemistry sequence. A 24-course UCR route using biology, geoscience, statistics and programming would have too little chemistry and would misrepresent the programme’s academic core.
exception.curriculumContext: The official prospective year-one page is labelled 2027–28 while the year-two and year-three pages are indicative 2026–27; these are a present programme structure cross-check, not a guaranteed cohort contract. Summing positive-credit items yields 60 EC in each year. Year-three 9 EC taught compulsory work plus 12 EC compulsory internship plus 39 EC elective room = 60 EC; 12 of the latter is restricted to Chemistry electives, with 27 EC free. The education minor is optional, and alternative chemistry electives are not simultaneously required.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked all 151 enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, profile/topic enrichment, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biochemical content and molecular lab work, while HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 introduce life science and cells. ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical/inorganic processes and recovery; ENSSUST112 and ENSSUST211 address materials life cycles and energy systems. DISGATE102, DISMATH211/214/314 and DISGATE101 provide some mathematical, statistical and programming support. None provides the laboratory and theory progression in chemical analysis, organic/inorganic synthesis, physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and quantum chemistry required to underpin this bachelor and its independent chemistry research internship. Isolated biochemical and environmental chemistry coverage cannot support a defensible 24-course Chemistry match.
